mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their prior 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive sequential revision in personal income (implied by PAYEMS and RSAFS growth acceleration) signals improved household balance sheets and higher consumption potential, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both show > 0.5% qoq growth acceleration
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for two consecutive months, combined with rising average hourly earnings (implied by HOUST and PAYEMS dynamics), signals a tight labor market and wage inflation, which raises input costs and may pressure margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 2 consecutive months AND HOUST growth > 1% qoq
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
